weeks.rationale: Peak week, 2 weeks out — the last week of real load before Hyrox, so we hold full in-band volume (~48 km) with three cleanly separated hard days: threshold Monday, a Hyrox compromised sim Wednesday, and a strength-endurance station circuit Friday. Heavy lower strength is clustered onto the hard threshold day to keep the easy days genuinely easy; plyometrics sit only on Thursday's easy run, which also now carries a dedicated heavy upper-body block (press + pull) - no running interference, invisible to Garmin load, and the last heavy-upper exposure before race week. Sunday is the fixed rest day.
weeks.methodology: Polarized distribution keeps the two easy runs genuinely easy (well below the ~139 Z2 ceiling, since LT1 was not measured) and concentrates quality into separated hard days. Threshold anchored on the measured LT2 (163 bpm / 4:34/km) raises the aerobic ceiling shared by Hyrox running and the 21k. Heavy low-rep strength drives running economy and sled power and, because concurrent interference is narrow, pairs safely with a hard run while plyometrics stay on an easy day. Compromised running at competition station loads supplies the race-specific stimulus. Upper-body pressing and pulling strength is programmed on the easy day for hybrid robustness and station economy, with no interference to running.

sessions.title: Threshold 5x6' + Heavy Lower (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (no-gym) THRESHOLD: 15 min easy warmup (Z1, <=138 bpm) -> 5x6 min @ threshold (155-163 bpm, 4:48-4:34/km) with 2:30 jog recovery -> 10 min easy cooldown. PM (gym, >=4 h later) HEAVY LOWER: back squat 4x3 @ 100 kg (RPE 8, explosive concentric, 3 min rest); trap-bar deadlift 3x3 @ 130 kg (RPE 8); hip thrust 3x8 @ 110 kg. No plyometrics today. Judge lifts by reps-in-reserve, not HR.
sessions.purpose: Raise LT2 and reinforce strength economy on one clean, unmistakably hard day.
sessions.why: Threshold is the highest-value running quality for both Hyrox and the 21k; pairing it with heavy (not explosive) lower strength clusters the hard feel and, per the narrow concurrent-interference window, does not blunt max strength. Kept to 5x6' rather than more to protect Wednesday's sim.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 55 min genuinely easy: HR <=138 bpm, ~5:35-6:00/km, fully conversational. Recovery from Monday's double — if in doubt, slow down.
sessions.purpose: Productive aerobic base at true easy intensity.
sessions.why: Easy volume is where aerobic fitness and the 21k base are built; keeping it genuinely easy protects the quality on Wednesday. No strides today so Monday's legs recover fully.

sessions.title: Hyrox Compromised Sim (5 rounds)
sessions.prescription: 10 min easy warmup -> 5 rounds, each: 1000 m run @ race pace (Z3-Z4, ~4:50-4:55/km, 150-160 bpm) straight into one station at Men's Pro load - R1 ski erg 1000 m; R2 sled push 202 kg / 50 m; R3 sled pull 153 kg / 50 m; R4 farmers carry 2x32 kg / 200 m; R5 wall balls 9 kg x 50. Minimal transitions. 5 min jog cooldown.
sessions.purpose: Rehearse race-pace running under station-induced fatigue across the full station spread.
sessions.why: Compromised running at competition loads is the core Hyrox specificity lever; five rounds is the peak-week dose while fresh, covering all the heavy stations without tipping into overload before race week.

sessions.title: Easy + Plyo + Heavy Upper (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (no-gym): 45 min easy, HR <=138 bpm, conversational. PM (gym) PLYO + HEAVY UPPER, judged by reps-in-reserve not HR: first while fresh - box jumps 4x3 + pogo hops 3x10, full recovery (CNS snap only). Then upper strength - weighted pull-up 4x4 (RPE 8); standing overhead press 4x4 (RPE 8); incline bench press 3x6 (RPE 7-8); chest-supported row 3x8 (RPE 8). Loads below are starting estimates - autoregulate to the target RPE and log actuals. Stop at RPE 8, not to failure - this is the last heavy-upper exposure before race week. Keep the plyo tiny so Thursday still buffers between Wednesday's sim and Friday's circuit.
sessions.purpose: Easy aerobic volume, explosive maintenance, and the week's dedicated upper-body strength between the two hard days.
sessions.why: Explosive work interferes with running only within the same hard session, so plyo stays on this easy day. Upper-body strength has effectively no running interference (the interference window is explosive lower-body power) and is invisible to Garmin load, so a full press+pull block slots here without disturbing the polarized running week; it backs the upper-biased Hyrox stations (ski erg, sled pull, wall ball, burpee broad jump). Placed as the last heavy-upper exposure before race week - held to RPE 8 with minimal plyo so Thursday still recovers between Wednesday's sim and Friday's circuit.

sessions.title: Strength-Endurance Station Circuit
sessions.prescription: 10 min easy warmup -> 4 rounds for quality, minimal rest within a round, 90 s between rounds: sandbag lunges 30 kg / 100 m; burpee broad jumps 15; wall balls 9 kg x 40; row 500 m; sled pull 153 kg / 25 m. -> 5 min easy jog. Station-endurance under fatigue, not a run day.
sessions.purpose: Local muscular endurance across the lighter stations at competition load.
sessions.why: Complements Wednesday's running-biased sim by loading the grip/leg/shoulder endurance the race demands; kept as a station circuit (little running) so it does not eat into the weekly km the easy runs carry.

sessions.title: Long Run + Race-Pace Finish
sessions.prescription: 75 min easy (HR <=140 bpm, ~5:35-5:50/km) -> 4x3 min @ race pace (~4:50-4:55/km) with 2 min easy jog between -> 6 min easy cooldown. Keep the bulk genuinely easy.
sessions.purpose: Aerobic endurance for the 21k base plus a short race-pace touch.
sessions.why: The long run is the primary endurance driver for the standing 21k goal; a short race-pace finish adds specificity without turning the run grey. Race-pace kept to 4x3' so it does not become a third hard running day.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Optional light mobility or an easy walk.
sessions.purpose: Recovery.
sessions.why: The fixed rest day protects recovery and separates the week's quality before race week begins.

weeks.rationale: Race week — Hyrox is Sunday 2 Aug. We train normally Monday through Wednesday (one sharpener, one short sim), then freshen the final three days: easy + openers Thursday, rest Friday, a short pre-race primer Saturday, race Sunday. No heavy strength this week so the legs arrive fresh; this is a deliberate half-week freshen, not a full-week taper.
weeks.methodology: A short freshen (volume down, intensity retained) preserves the fitness built in the block while shedding fatigue — the athlete's chosen abbreviation of the classic taper, justified by the shorter Hyrox effort and an err-high bias. The final sharpeners stay at race pace to keep the neuromuscular system primed. Heavy strength and plyometrics are dropped in the freshen window to avoid residual leg fatigue.

sessions.title: Race-Pace Sharpener 5x1000 m
sessions.prescription: 15 min easy warmup -> 5x1000 m @ race-to-threshold pace (~4:45-4:55/km, 155-163 bpm) with 2 min jog recovery -> 10 min easy cooldown. Crisp and controlled, not maximal.
sessions.purpose: Sharpen race-pace turnover early in race week while there is still time to absorb it.
sessions.why: Race-pace intervals keep the aerobic-power system primed; placed Monday (6 days out) so any fatigue clears well before Sunday. No accompanying strength this week to keep the legs fresh.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 45 min genuinely easy, HR <=138 bpm, conversational. Pure recovery between the two race-week quality touches.
sessions.purpose: Easy aerobic flush.
sessions.why: Keeps blood flowing and aerobic base ticking while shedding Monday's fatigue; strictly easy so Wednesday's sim is sharp.

sessions.title: Short Hyrox Primer (3 rounds)
sessions.prescription: 10 min easy warmup -> 3 rounds: 1000 m run @ race pace (~4:50-4:55/km) into one station - R1 sled push 202 kg / 50 m; R2 sled pull 153 kg / 50 m; R3 wall balls 9 kg x 40. Controlled, rehearse transitions. 5 min jog cooldown.
sessions.purpose: Final race-specific rehearsal at low volume — transitions and race feel, not fitness building.
sessions.why: Three rounds keeps the race pattern fresh in the legs while the reduced volume begins the freshen; the last true station work before the race.

sessions.title: Easy + Openers
sessions.prescription: 30 min easy (HR <=138 bpm) + 4x20 s relaxed strides at race pace with full walk-back recovery. Freshen begins: short and snappy, never draining.
sessions.purpose: Maintain leg speed with minimal fatigue as the freshen starts.
sessions.why: Strides keep neuromuscular pop without cost; volume drops sharply now that the race is 3 days out.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Light mobility and good sleep. Rest day shifted from Sunday this week for the race.
sessions.purpose: Freshen — shed all residual fatigue.
sessions.why: A full rest 2 days out banks recovery for race day; the usual Sunday rest moves here because Sunday is race day.

sessions.title: Pre-Race Primer
sessions.prescription: 15 min easy jog + 3x30 s at race pace (~4:50/km) with full recovery + a few dynamic drills. Just enough to feel sharp for tomorrow — leave completely fresh.
sessions.purpose: Prime the system the day before the race without adding fatigue.
sessions.why: A short opener with a few race-pace touches wakes the legs up; kept under 25 min so it primes rather than tires.

sessions.title: RACE: Hyrox
sessions.prescription: RACE DAY. 8x1000 m running interspersed with the 8 stations (ski erg, sled push 202 kg, sled pull 153 kg, burpee broad jumps, row, farmers 2x32 kg, sandbag lunges 30 kg, wall balls 100). Pace the first 2-3 runs conservatively (~4:55-5:00/km), hold form through the sleds, empty the tank on the last run + wall balls.

steps.target: even pacing, controlled sleds, strong final 1 km

sessions.purpose: Race the first Hyrox of the calendar.
sessions.why: The target the whole block pointed at; execution over heroics — bank a solid time and a clean data point to shape the Nov 14 build.

weeks.rationale: Post-race week, first week of the Nov 14 base build (15 weeks out). Per your preference we take a single easy recovery day Monday, then train through in-band the rest of the week — not a full recovery week. Emphasis shifts to aerobic volume with one moderate quality touch and a return to heavy strength; nothing peaked. If the race leaves you beaten up, ask and I'll soften Wednesday/Thursday.
weeks.methodology: Base phase prioritizes easy aerobic volume to rebuild the engine for the 21k and the next Hyrox, with sparing intensity. A single recovery day respects race stress without detraining. Heavy strength returns for running economy; it is placed to make a clean hard day rather than blunting an easy one. Long-run volume climbs back toward base.

sessions.title: Active Recovery
sessions.prescription: Very easy 20-30 min: walk, easy spin, or mobility + light stretching. No running, no load. The one recovery day after the race.
sessions.purpose: Flush race-day fatigue and soreness.
sessions.why: One low-stress day clears the worst of the race DOMS so the rest of the week can be productive; more than a day off is unnecessary at your recovery bias.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 50 min easy, HR <=138 bpm, conversational. First run back — ease in, cut short if the legs are still heavy.
sessions.purpose: Re-establish easy aerobic rhythm.
sessions.why: Gentle re-entry to running after the race; easy volume rebuilds the base without stressing legs that just raced.

sessions.title: Tempo 3x8'
sessions.prescription: 15 min easy warmup -> 3x8 min @ tempo (147-155 bpm, 5:04-4:48/km) with 2 min jog -> 10 min easy cooldown. Tempo, not threshold — controlled first quality back.
sessions.purpose: Reintroduce sustained aerobic-threshold work at a controlled intensity.
sessions.why: Tempo rather than full threshold eases quality back in the week after a race; still enough stimulus to hold the aerobic ceiling built for Hyrox.

sessions.title: Heavy Lower + Easy Shakeout (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (no-gym): 20 min very easy shakeout, HR <=135 bpm. PM (gym): back squat 4x3 @ 100 kg (RPE 8, 3 min rest); trap-bar deadlift 3x3 @ 130 kg; hip thrust 3x8 @ 110 kg; weighted step-up 3x8 @ 20 kg/hand. Judge by RIR, not HR. No plyometrics.
sessions.purpose: Restore heavy strength for running economy and sled power in the new build.
sessions.why: Heavy low-rep strength is the main economy driver; reintroduced now to anchor the 15-week Hyrox build. Paired with only a light shakeout so it is a clean strength day.

sessions.title: Easy + Strides
sessions.prescription: 50 min easy (HR <=138 bpm) + 6x20 s relaxed strides with full recovery. Easy volume with a light neuromuscular touch.
sessions.purpose: Aerobic volume plus economy pop.
sessions.why: Builds base km toward the 47-58 target; strides add turnover without grey-zone cost the day before the long run.

sessions.title: Long Run
sessions.prescription: 100 min steady easy, HR <=142 bpm, ~5:30-5:50/km throughout. Pure aerobic long run — no surges this week, just time on feet rebuilding the 21k base.
sessions.purpose: Aerobic endurance for the 21k and the Hyrox base.
sessions.why: The long run is the primary endurance driver; kept purely easy the week after a race to build volume without adding intensity stress.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Optional light mobility or an easy walk.
sessions.purpose: Recovery.
sessions.why: The fixed weekly rest day, back in its normal Sunday slot now the race is done.

weeks.rationale: Base build, 14 weeks to Hyrox #2. A full in-band base week (~50 km) with quality reintroduced: one true threshold session (paired with heavy lower to make a clean hard day) and one base-level compromised sim to keep race skills alive. Everything else is easy aerobic volume; Sunday rest. This is engine-building, not peaking.
weeks.methodology: Base phase leans on large easy volume with sparing high-quality threshold to raise LT2 — the shared lever for the 21k and Hyrox running. Heavy strength continues for economy and is clustered onto the threshold day so easy days stay easy; plyometrics sit on an easy day. A single moderate sim maintains compromised-running skill far out from the race without the specificity load of a peak block.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 55 min easy, HR <=138 bpm, conversational. Sets up the week's first quality on Tuesday.
sessions.purpose: Easy aerobic base.
sessions.why: Opens the week with genuinely easy volume so Tuesday's threshold is sharp; easy running is where the aerobic base is built.

sessions.title: Threshold 4x8' + Heavy Lower (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (no-gym) THRESHOLD: 15 min easy warmup -> 4x8 min @ threshold (155-163 bpm, 4:48-4:34/km) with 2:30 jog -> 10 min easy cooldown. PM (gym): back squat 4x3 @ 100 kg (RPE 8, progress if >2 RIR); trap-bar deadlift 3x3 @ 130 kg; hip thrust 3x8 @ 110 kg. No plyometrics today.
sessions.purpose: Raise LT2 and maintain strength economy in one clean hard day.
sessions.why: Threshold volume nudged up to 4x8' as base fitness rebuilds; paired with heavy lower to cluster the hard feel. Progress the squat load if it leaves >2 RIR — that is the fix for it feeling easy.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 50 min genuinely easy, HR <=138 bpm. Recovery between the week's two hard days.
sessions.purpose: Easy recovery volume.
sessions.why: Separates Tuesday's threshold from Thursday's sim with a truly easy day, protecting both.

sessions.title: Base Compromised Sim (4 rounds)
sessions.prescription: 10 min easy warmup -> 4 rounds: 1000 m run @ race pace (~4:55/km, 150-160 bpm) into one station - R1 ski erg 1000 m; R2 sled push 202 kg / 50 m; R3 farmers carry 2x32 kg / 200 m; R4 wall balls 9 kg x 50. 5 min jog cooldown.
sessions.purpose: Maintain compromised-running skill and station endurance far out from the race.
sessions.why: Four rounds keeps the race pattern alive during base without the specificity load of a peak sim; a lighter dose than the peak-week five rounds since the race is 14 weeks away.

sessions.title: Easy + Plyo Primer (double)
sessions.prescription: AM (no-gym): 45 min easy, HR <=138 bpm. PM (gym, ~15 min): box jumps 4x3 + hurdle hops 3x5, full recovery. Explosive snap only.
sessions.purpose: Easy volume plus explosive maintenance.
sessions.why: Plyometrics preserve power for sleds and running economy; kept on an easy day per the concurrent-interference window, and the run stays easy before Saturday's long run.

sessions.title: Long Run + Race-Pace Finish
sessions.prescription: 80 min easy (HR <=142 bpm, ~5:30-5:50/km) -> 4x3 min @ race pace (~4:55/km) with 2 min easy jog -> 6 min easy cooldown.
sessions.purpose: Build 21k endurance with a light race-pace touch.
sessions.why: Long-run volume climbs as base builds; the short race-pace finish keeps specificity without a third hard running day.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Optional light mobility or an easy walk.
sessions.purpose: Recovery.
sessions.why: The fixed weekly rest day; protects recovery and closes the block cleanly.
